correctness.rationale: For all integers n≥5, open Lovász neighborhood complex of R_{3,n}=K3 square Kn is the union of Yi, three row-centered simplex unions. Each Yi has the nerve boundary of an (n−1)-simplex and is S^{n−2}; pairwise intersections are a connected crown graph K_{n,n} minus its matching, H1 rank n²−3n+1, plus n isolated vertices in the third row; triple intersection is 3n isolated vertices. The integral homological Čech double complex has E1_{2,0}=Z^{3n}, E1_{1,0}=Z^{3(n+1)}, E1_{0,0}=Z³. The triple-to-pairs differential projects to an explicit signed 3n×3n permutation matrix on the isolated-coordinate summand, hence split injective over Z; ∂1 rank two, so the residual degree-one term is Z without torsion. The crown H1 terms contribute 3(n²−3n+1) two-classes; the Yi yield three degree-(n−2) classes. No d2 source survives and free graded quotients split, giving H1=Z, H2=Z^{3n²−9n+3}, H_{n−2}=Z³, none other. Independent full-face mod2 calculations at n=5,6,7 confirm ranks and combinatorial intersections; the all-n and integral conclusions are from the exact symbolic split-injection proof.

originality.rationale: Shukla’s classification restricts to graphs of max degree at most 3 or selected 4-regular circulants, whereas the rook graph has degree n+1. The closest published all-m,n rook open-neighborhood result computes relative quotient and H_k for k>=3 but explicitly leaves low H1/H2 unresolved; it supplies high H_{n-2} when n>=5 but not the two low groups. The present complete integral low-degree determination is therefore an original substantive refinement, with risk of unindexed rook tables.

value.rationale: Open Lovász neighborhood complexes of rook graphs are a canonical graph-topological family with chromatic/topological motivation. Determining all integral groups, including low-dimensional attaching effects and torsion-freeness for the infinite three-row range, fills a precise gap left by known high-dimensional computations. The signed isolated-component minor is a structural lemma, not a known-table recomputation.
